newsitem.title: USA: Democrat seeks to invalidate results in Texas race.
newsitem.headline: Democrat seeks to invalidate results in Texas race.

text.p: A Democrat who ran third behind U.S. Representative Ken Bentsen and a Republican challenger in the race for Houston's congressional seat asked a federal court panel Wednesday to invalidate the Nov. 5 election results.

The court challenge by Beverley Clark, a former Houston city councilwoman, took place as early voting began Wednesday for a Dec. 10 runoff election between incumbent Ken Bentsen and Republican Dolly Madison McKenna.
Clark fell 200 votes shy of winning a spot on the ballot for the runoff between incumbent Bentsen, also a Democrat, and Republican McKenna in Texas' 25th Congressional District.

Clark's lawyer, Houston attorney Kenneth Wynne, said voters were confused by a special ballot that included names of two Democrats and eight Republicans in the race and gave conflicting instructions on straight-party voting.
Bentsen is a nephew of former U.S. Sen. and Treasury Secretary Lloyd Bentsen, also of Texas.

His congressional district was one of 11 in Texas redrawn by a three-judge federal panel after three districts in the state were ruled unconstitutional because of racial gerrymandering. The court decision opened elections in the redrawn districts to all comers.

Of the more than 128,000 votes cast in the election, 35,786 were invalidated because voters apparently overlooked a special teal-coloured ballot used for the U.S. House of Representatives race or chose more than one candidate on the ballot, Wynne said.
"Clark needed less than two percent of those (invalidated) votes to be in the run-off with Bentsen," Wynne said.

Clark filed her challenge with the three-judge federal panel that redrew the Texas districts and ordered the special primary voting in November. On Tuesday, she filed a lawsuit in state court seeking to overturn the election.
Runoff elections were also set for Dec. 10 in two other Texas districts where a candidate failed to capture a majority.
